QR Codes for Restaurants, Cafes and Bars

A few well-placed QR codes save your staff time and give guests menus, WiFi and a way to leave a review without asking. Here is what works and how to set it up.

Use Cases

Where QR codes help a restaurant

Digital menu

Link a PDF or web menu on table tents, windows and takeout bags. See the QR code menu generator.

WiFi for guests

Put a WiFi code on tables or the counter. See the WiFi QR code generator.

Google reviews

Ask happy guests for a review on the receipt. See the Google review QR code.

Feedback form

A short form on the table catches problems before they become public. Use a Google Forms QR code.

Social follow

A code on the counter grows your Instagram or Facebook. Try Instagram or Facebook.

Table numbers

Give each table its own code with the number in the link, using the bulk QR code generator.

Setting up a QR code menu

The menu code is the one most guests will use, so it is worth getting right.

  1. Publish your menu as a mobile-friendly web page or a small PDF on your website.
  2. Make a static QR code that points to that address, and keep the address the same forever.
  3. When prices or dishes change, update the page or file, not the code.
  4. Put "Scan for menu" next to the code.
  5. Test on an iPhone and an Android phone, in the dining room's lighting.

Best practices

A few habits decide whether guests enjoy QR codes or resent them.

  • Keep a paper option. Some guests prefer not to scan, and older guests may need help.
  • Keep menus light. A heavy PDF loads slowly on weak restaurant WiFi. Compress images.
  • Print at least 3 cm (1.2 in) on table tents. See the size guide.
  • Show allergens clearly in the menu itself.
  • Protect the codes. Check tables regularly for stickers placed over your codes. See QR code safety.
  • Do not put guest passwords or payment logins behind a scan unless you control the page.

Getting more reviews the right way

A review code on the receipt or table is a natural way to collect Google reviews from happy guests. Ask everyone, not just the ones who seem satisfied, and never offer a discount or gift in exchange for a review, because review platforms prohibit incentives.
